payload.text: Director Vance — the consolidated briefing-and-notice record is linked to the published OARI packet so the venue, the notice dates, the public numbers and the access arrangements can be checked directly instead of anyone repeating the briefing. What is on that record: the D3 community briefing convened in Fruitvale in daylight, the notice dates as issued, the Fruitvale response-time and San Antonio comparison figures as published, and the access arrangements made for people who could not attend in person. The packet carries OARI as dispatch-live with $10,817,307.66 remaining and renewable, next step due C117 — the record now sits beside that, not behind it. If a line is missing from the link, name it and I will supply it from the district file rather than have your office reconstruct it.

Director Vance — the records you are asking for are the district's briefing and transit-review notice records, and here is what I can put on the record plainly. The D3 East Oakland community briefing was scheduled in Fruitvale, in daylight, with the Fruitvale data and response times on the table, and the residents who were promised access were told where and when. On the OARI venue: the briefing was held at a Fruitvale neighborhood venue, not an East Oakland site, and I will say that plainly rather than let the notice read as if the venue were something it was not — that choice was mine, made so the Fruitvale data could be walked through with the people it describes. The transit-review notices went out through the Fruitvale Transit Hub intake channel, and Delia Vargas-Ruiz, the Transit Hub D3 intake liaison, is the named contact for any resident who says they did not receive one. What I am committing to: the venue, the notice dates, and the access provided will be written into a single district record so no resident has to take my word for it, and the Fruitvale review stays open to San Antonio and East Oakland residents on the same terms. If any notice did not land, the intake channel is where I want it reported so it can be fixed rather than argued about.

all.sourceText:
## Rose Delgado — City Council District 3

- **Agent:** `.claude/agents/civic-office-council-d3/`
- **Address:** Introduce District 3's community benefit stipulations for the Baylight Phase II RFP process to protect surrounding West Oakland and Jack London commercial corridors.
- **Why:** District 3 experienced a 7-point approval drop (83, -7) in C104 following the C103 shortlist release, while West Oakland retail vitality remains at 3.52.
- **Acceptance:** Formal submission of District 3 priority terms regarding local business contracting and infrastructure linkages for the Baylight Phase II RFP.
- **Silence consequence:** Baylight procurement proceeds without enforceable D3 community protections, deepening commercial disparities in neighboring corridors.
